items.title: Trump won't rule out ground troops in Iran as strikes enter third day

featured_image.name: Donald Trump won't rule out boots on ground in Iran

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Monday declined to rule out deploying American ground forces to Iran, telling the New York Post he would send them "if necessary" as U.S. and Israeli military operations against Iran continued into their third day under Operation Epic Fury.[1]

"I don't have the yips with respect to boots on the ground — like every president says, 'There will be no boots on the ground.' I don't say it," Trump told the Post. "I say 'probably don't need them,' [or] 'if they were necessary.'"[2][1]

At the Pentagon, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth struck a similar tone during the first detailed briefing since the operation began on Saturday, refusing to specify what the administration would or would not do. "President Trump ensures that our enemies understand we'll go as far as we need to go to advance American interests," Hegseth said, appearing alongside Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine.[3][4]

items.title: Six US troops killed as Trump won't rule out ground forces in Iran

featured_image.name: War in the Mideast widens as Trump says strikes on Iran ...

items.description:
The United States is "not currently postured" to send ground forces into Iran, Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters on Monday, even as President Donald Trump refused to take the option off the table and the American military campaign entered its third day with mounting casualties on both sides.[1][2]

Rubio, speaking on Capitol Hill before briefing the congressional "Gang of Eight," said the administration is confident its objectives can be achieved through air and naval power alone. But in comments to the New York Post, Trump struck a different tone: "Probably don't need them," he said of ground troops, adding, "if they were necessary" — a stark departure from the traditional presidential assurance of "no boots on the ground."[3][4]

items.title: Iranian drones strike US Embassy in Riyadh, sparking fire

featured_image.name: Fire at US embassy complex in Riyadh after blast heard ...

items.description: A fire erupted at the U.S. Embassy in Riyadh early Tuesday after two suspected Iranian drones struck the compound, according to a U.S. State Department cable reviewed by The Wall Street Journal. There were no immediate reports of injuries, and embassy personnel sheltered in place.[1][2]

items.title: Saudi Arabia goes on full military alert after Iranian drone strikes

featured_image.name: Return to Your Senses': Gulf States Ramp Up Iran Criticism ...

items.description:
Saudi Arabia raised its military readiness to "full alert" on Monday after Iranian drones struck the massive Ras Tanura refinery on the kingdom's Gulf coast, as the Gulf Cooperation Council condemned Tehran's attacks across six member states and warned it reserves the right to retaliate.[1][2]

The escalation came three days into a widening Middle East conflict that began on February 28 when the United States and Israel launched airstrikes against Iran. Tehran responded with volleys of missiles and drones targeting GCC nations that host American military installations, killing at least six people and injuring more than 100 across the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, and Saudi Arabia.[3][2]

items.title: Ukraine says it recaptured more land than Russia seized in February

featured_image.name: Ukraine's military makes gains in southeast region of ...

items.description:
Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi announced on March 2 that Ukrainian defense forces reclaimed more territory in February than Russian troops managed to seize — the first time Kyiv has outpaced Moscow in territorial gains since the Kursk Oblast incursion into Russian territory in the summer of 2024.[1][2]

"In February 2026, for the first time since the Kursk offensive operation, the Ukrainian defence forces regained control of more territory than the enemy managed to capture," Syrskyi wrote on Telegram. "We have survived this difficult battle for winter."[2][1]

items.title: Rubio says Israel's strike plan triggered US attack on Iran

featured_image.name: US says Rubio to visit Israel on Monday to discuss Iran ...

items.description:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio disclosed Monday that the United States launched its attack on Iran after learning that Israel was determined to strike with or without American participation, a revelation that cast the joint military operation in a new light and raised fresh questions about the administration's legal justification for war.

"We knew that there was going to be an Israeli action. We knew that that would precipitate an attack against American forces, and we knew that if we didn't preemptively go after them before they launched those attacks, we would suffer higher casualties," Rubio told reporters on Capitol Hill before briefing congressional leaders.[1][2]

items.title: Trump refuses to rule out ground troops in Iran

featured_image.name: What is Trump's approval rating? Iran strikes controversial in polls

items.description:
President Donald Trump said Monday he would not rule out sending American ground troops into Iran, declaring that Operation Epic Fury is progressing faster than expected as the U.S. military campaign entered its third day with mounting casualties on both sides.

"I don't have the yips with respect to boots on the ground — like every president says, 'There will be no boots on the ground.' I don't say it," Trump told the New York Post in an interview published March 2. "I say 'probably don't need them,' or 'if they were necessary.'"[1][2]

items.title: Six US troops killed in Iranian strike on Kuwait base

featured_image.name: At least three US service members killed during Iran ...

items.description:
An Iranian strike on a makeshift military operations center at a civilian port in Kuwait has killed six American service members, marking the first US casualties since the start of Operation Epic Fury against Iran on Saturday.

The death toll climbed throughout the day Monday as military teams worked to recover remains from the burning facility. US Central Command initially reported three service members killed in action on Sunday, then confirmed a fourth had succumbed to injuries early Monday morning. By Monday afternoon, CENTCOM announced the recovery of two additional service members' remains from the struck facility, bringing the total to six killed.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Antarctica lost nearly 5,000 square miles of ice in 30 years, study finds

featured_image.name: Experts issue warning as powerful Antarctic phenomenon reaches ...

items.description: A comprehensive 30-year satellite analysis has revealed that Antarctica's ice sheet has lost 12,820 square kilometers — nearly 5,000 square miles — of grounded ice since 1996, an area roughly equivalent to 10 cities the size of Greater Los Angeles. The findings, published Monday in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, offer the first complete mapping of Antarctica's grounding line across the entire continent over such a long time span.[1][2]

items.title: State Dept. tells Americans to 'depart now' from 14 Middle East nations

featured_image.name: Warning Issued to Americans in 14 Countries as Iran War Grows—'Depart Now'

items.description:
The U.S. State Department on Monday issued an urgent advisory calling on American citizens to "depart now" from more than a dozen countries across the Middle East, as U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran entered their third day with no signs of slowing.[1][2]

Assistant Secretary of State for Consular Affairs Mora Namdar posted the warning on X, listing Bahrain, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Israel, the West Bank and Gaza, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Syria, the United Arab Emirates, and Yemen as countries Americans should leave immediately using commercial means "due to significant safety concerns".[3][1]

items.title: Israel launches new airstrikes on Tehran as war enters third day

featured_image.name: War in Middle East widens as Israeli and U.S. planes pound Iran and Tehran and its proxies hit back

items.description:
The Israeli military announced late Monday that it had begun a fresh series of airstrikes on Tehran, targeting Iranian regime installations as the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran entered its third day with no signs of abating.[1][2]

The strikes followed an evacuation warning issued by the IDF's Persian-language spokesman, Lt. Col. Kamal Penhasi, urging residents in Tehran's Evin neighborhood to immediately leave areas near the headquarters of state broadcaster IRIB. Israel's Channel 12 reported that Iranian state television facilities were among the targets in the latest wave of attacks.[3][4]

items.title: Satellite images reveal vast damage to Iran's military sites

featured_image.name: Satellite Images Show Collapsed Tunnels, Aftermath of Iran Strikes

items.description:
Commercial satellite imagery collected in the days following joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran has provided an unprecedented look at the scale of destruction inflicted on military installations stretching from the country's southeastern coast to its northwestern mountains.

Images captured on March 1 and March 2 by U.S. spatial intelligence firm Vantor and Planet Labs show burning warships, collapsed tunnel entrances, obliterated drone facilities, and flattened radar systems at sites across the country. The imagery offers the clearest visual accounting yet of what American officials have described as Operation Epic Fury, launched on February 28 in coordination with Israel.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Israel to reopen Kerem Shalom crossing for Gaza aid

featured_image.name: Aid trucks pass through Kerem Shalom crossing enroute to Gaza

items.description: Israel announced Monday that it will reopen the Kerem Shalom border crossing with Gaza starting Tuesday for the gradual entry of humanitarian aid, according to COGAT, the Israeli military body that oversees civilian affairs in the Palestinian territories. The decision comes after all crossings into Gaza were shut on Saturday as Israeli and U.S. forces launched joint military strikes on Iran.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Bolivia raids homes to recover cash looted from deadly plane crash

featured_image.name: Bolivia cargo plane crash near El Alto leaves casualties and ...

items.description:
Bolivian security forces have raided at least 22 homes near the site where a military cargo plane carrying tens of millions of dollars in newly printed banknotes crashed last week, as authorities work to recover money looted from the wreckage of one of the country's deadliest aviation disasters in years.[1]

The raids follow the February 27 crash of a Bolivian Air Force C-130 Hercules transport plane at El Alto International Airport, which killed at least 22 people — most of them civilians on the ground — and injured dozens more. The aircraft, arriving from Santa Cruz, was carrying 18 tons of freshly printed currency worth an estimated 423 million bolivianos, roughly $62 million, on behalf of the Central Bank of Bolivia.[2][3][4][5]

items.title: SpaceX's Starship V3 debut slips to April as testing advances

featured_image.name: Starship Booster 19 survives the cryo test, Flight 12 ...

items.description: SpaceX is in the final stages of preparing its first Starship Version 3 vehicle for flight, though the timeline for what the company calls Flight 12 appears to be shifting from a March target to no earlier than April 7, according to recent FCC filings and launch tracking data.[1][2]

items.title: Putin calls Gulf leaders as Iran conflict widens

featured_image.name: In Russia, UAE leader calls for dialogue to end Ukraine war

items.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke by phone with UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on Monday to discuss the rapidly escalating military conflict in the Middle East, as the Kremlin positioned itself as a potential mediator between Tehran and the Gulf states caught in the crossfire of U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran.

The call, confirmed by the UAE state news agency WAM, came as Moscow said it remained in "constant contact" with Iran's leadership and was engaged in ongoing dialogue with Persian Gulf states affected by the widening conflict.[1][2]

items.title: Pentagon told Congress Iran showed no signs of attacking US first, sources say

featured_image.name: Pentagon Presses Iran Strike Claims as Briefed Senators ...

items.description:
The United States and Israel launched a sweeping joint military offensive against Iran on February 28, 2026, striking more than 1,000 targets across the country in what the Pentagon designated Operation Epic Fury and Israel called Operation Roaring Lion. The campaign killed Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and dozens of senior officials, marking the most ambitious U.S.-Israeli military action in decades.[1][2]

As operations entered their third day on Monday, the assault showed no sign of slowing, with President Donald Trump warning that strikes could continue for "four weeks or as long as necessary". The Pentagon, however, faced mounting scrutiny after administration officials acknowledged in closed-door congressional briefings that there was no intelligence suggesting Iran had planned to attack U.S. forces first.[3][4][5]

items.title: Qatar shoots down two Iranian jets in Gulf first

featured_image.name: Qatar air force shoots down two aircraft from Iran: Defence ...

items.description:
Qatar's air force shot down two Iranian Sukhoi Su-24 fighter jets on Monday, marking the first time a Gulf country has engaged a manned Iranian aircraft since Tehran began its retaliatory bombardment of the region three days ago. The Qatari Defense Ministry said its forces also intercepted seven ballistic missiles and five drones, with all projectiles neutralized before reaching their intended targets.[1][2][3]

The shootdowns came on the third day of Iranian strikes across the Persian Gulf, launched in retaliation for joint US-Israeli attacks on Iran that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on February 28. Iran has targeted multiple Gulf states hosting US military assets, turning the skies over Doha, Dubai, Manama, and Kuwait City into active conflict zones.[4][5][6][7]

items.title: Trump says Iran war likely to last at least a month

featured_image.name: WATCH LIVE: Trump may address war with Iran at Medal of Honor ceremony

items.description:
President Trump used a Medal of Honor ceremony at the White House on Monday to deliver his first live public remarks on the U.S.-led military campaign against Iran, warning that operations could last four to five weeks and acknowledging that more American casualties are likely as the conflict enters its third day.[1][2]

The president spoke after awarding the Medal of Honor to three U.S. Army soldiers — Master Sergeant Roderick W. Edmonds, honored posthumously for protecting Jewish prisoners of war during World War II; Staff Sergeant Michael H. Ollis, honored posthumously for his heroism in Afghanistan; and Command Sergeant Major Terry P. Richardson, a retired Vietnam War veteran. The juxtaposition of honoring past military valor with the reality of a new armed conflict lent the ceremony an unusual gravity.[3][4]

items.title: Macron offers to station French nuclear weapons in Europe

featured_image.name: Reading between the lines of the new France-UK nuclear ...

items.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron declared on Monday that France will increase the size of its nuclear arsenal and strengthen its deterrence posture, warning that the world faces a growing risk of conflicts crossing the nuclear threshold. Speaking from the Île Longue submarine base in Brittany — home to France's four ballistic missile submarines — Macron described the current era as one of "geopolitical turmoil filled with dangers" and called for a "fortification" of France's deterrence.[1]

The address, closely watched by European allies, marks the most consequential shift in French nuclear doctrine in decades. Macron introduced a concept of "forward deterrence" and, for the first time, formally offered to station French nuclear weapons in other European nations, following a model long used by the United States, which maintains warheads in Germany, Belgium, Italy, and Turkey under NATO sharing arrangements.[2][3]
